name: @vibeinfra/mcp-server

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List every incident simulation and course in the VibeInfra catalog. Each entry includes its difficulty tier, tech stack, expected duration and a link to its landing page. Use this to see what is available; use search_incidents to narrow by topic.

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag, e.g. 'id'. Untranslated courses fall back to English.

free_only.description: Only incidents that are free to run.

tools.name: search_incidents
tools.description: Find incident simulations by free-text query and/or by difficulty, category, domain, tech stack or free-to-run status. The query matches the title, description, category and tech stack. Returns the same summary shape as list_incidents.

query.description: Free text, e.g. 'kafka consumer lag' or 'certificate expiry'.

free_only.description: Only incidents that are free to run.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Fetch the full blueprint for one incident by catalog ID (for example 'incident-22-k8s-crashloop'), including its learning objectives, chapters where the course is step-graded, tech stack and access tier. IDs come from list_incidents.

tools.name: get_platform_capacity
tools.description: Read how much VibeInfra sandbox capacity is in use right now and how many learners are queued. Worth checking before telling a user to start a lab: when the queue is long, a start request is queued rather than provisioned immediately.

tools.name: lookup_infrastructure_term
tools.description: Look up infrastructure and SRE terminology in the VibeInfra glossary — the same definitions used across the incident catalog. Omit the term to return the whole glossary.

term.description: Term to look up. Matched case-insensitively against labels and IDs.

tools.name: start_drill
tools.description: Provision and launch a live disposable sandbox for an SRE incident simulation. Returns the active session_id, web terminal URL, objectives, and scenario briefing. When finished, evaluate your fix with grade_drill.

course_id.description: Catalog ID of the incident simulation, e.g. 'incident-40-deployment-never-rolled-out'.

force_fresh.description: If true, terminates any existing sandbox and boots a fresh container.

tools.name: get_drill_hint
tools.description: Fetch spoiler-free progressive guidance for an active incident session. Provides diagnostic nudges without revealing the direct solution.

session_id.description: Active session ID returned by start_drill.

tools.name: grade_drill
tools.description: Run automated system-state evaluation against the live sandbox to verify if the incident has been resolved. Inspects kernel sockets, container states, and ingress health. Returns pass/fail status, completed steps, and earned XP.

session_id.description: Active session ID returned by start_drill.

course_id.description: Catalog ID of the incident simulation (optional; automatically resolved from session).

tools.name: get_drill_status
tools.description: Inspect real-time telemetry, node health statuses, and network topology for an active drill session.

session_id.description: Active session ID returned by start_drill.

tools.name: stop_drill
tools.description: Permanently terminates and tears down the disposable sandbox container for a completed or aborted session.

tools.name: exec_in_sandbox
tools.description: Run an arbitrary diagnostic, triage, or remediation command directly inside the live container sandbox. Returns stdout, stderr, and exit_code. Enables headless incident troubleshooting without opening a browser.

session_id.description: Active session ID returned by start_drill.

command.description: Shell command to execute, e.g. 'kubectl get pods -A', 'df -h', 'systemctl status nginx'.

timeout_sec.description: Command execution timeout in seconds (default 15, max 30).

timeout_seconds.description: Command execution timeout in seconds (alias for timeout_sec).

instructions: VibeInfra is an incident-readiness platform for infrastructure engineers: engineers troubleshoot realistic production incidents (Linux kernel, Docker, Kubernetes, Nginx, PostgreSQL, Kafka, AWS) in live disposable sandboxes with automated grading. Use these tools to discover incidents, start live incident drills (start_drill), coach learners with progressive hints without spoilers (get_drill_hint), inspect live telemetry/topology (get_drill_status), and grade fixes against the live system state (grade_drill).
